head: 19e3b23
target: Repos opt into the gate with a tracked .own-your-diff marker: quizgate sync distributes the gate to a stable PATH location and installs a pre-push hook in every opted-in clone, replacing the core.hooksPath + repo-carried .githooks design.
incidental: selftest moved from skills/own-your-diff/scripts/ to scripts/ (pure rename), and its SKILL.md bullet dropped
quizgate usage text for the new install and sync commands
agent-mode.md wording on spawning fresh examiner subagents

questions.prompt: Why does the repo opt in with a tracked .own-your-diff marker instead of the old core.hooksPath=.githooks design?

options.label: The marker itself enforces the gate: git blocks pushes from any clone that carries it, even with no plugin installed
core.hooksPath no longer works in current git, so a config-based opt-in became impossible
The marker is tracked content, so it arrives with every clone and sync can install the hook there automatically; core.hooksPath is clone-local config that never travels
A .githooks directory tracked in the repo cannot contain a pre-push hook

key_points: git config such as core.hooksPath is clone-local: it never travels with a clone, so the old design needed a manual install step in every fresh clone
a tracked marker arrives with the clone, so the session hook's sync detects it and installs the pre-push hook automatically, with no human step
the marker is an opt-in signal, not enforcement: a clone without the plugin has no hook and pushes ungated
side effects: the repo no longer carries a .githooks dir and no per-clone git config is mutated

questions.prompt: The installed pre-push hook runs quizgate resolved from PATH (falling back to ~/.local/bin/quizgate) instead of calling the script inside the plugin's install directory. What does that boundary buy?

options.label: Git refuses to execute a hook that calls a script outside the repository
The plugin's install directory is wiped at the end of every session
The hook stays a stable shim: the plugin's install path can move on update, and sync keeps a fresh quizgate at the stable location the hook resolves to

key_points: a hook that pinned the plugin's install path would break whenever the plugin updates and moves its files
sync refreshes a copy at a stable, conventional location (~/.local/bin by default) in every session, matching the hook's fallback
command -v runs first, so an existing quizgate on PATH wins and the design composes with other installs

questions.prompt: A clone already has the hook installed. Which of these hold when things go wrong? Pick all that apply.

options.label: quizgate is gone from PATH and ~/.local/bin at push time: the push is blocked with a message pointing to the project, not silently allowed
quizgate is gone at push time: the push goes through, since there is nothing left to enforce the gate
A foreign pre-push hook already exists and you run install: it refuses to touch the hook and prints the line to add
A foreign pre-push hook already exists when sync runs: the session is unaffected and the hook is left alone

key_points: an installed gate fails closed: a missing quizgate blocks the push with an install pointer, never a silent pass, because a silent no-op would let unquizzed work through while the gate is believed active
write_hook never clobbers a foreign hook: it refuses and prints the line to add, and install fails loudly because a human is there to act
sync runs automatically in every session, so it must never be fatal: it skips what it cannot do and leaves the hook alone

questions.prompt: A maintainer decides this repo should drop the gate: they delete the tracked .own-your-diff marker and commit. What state do existing clones stay in, what happens on their next push of new, unquizzed work, and where would a fix for the gap go?
key_points: hooks are per-clone state: the marker only drives installation, and nothing removes a hook when the marker disappears
existing clones keep the installed hook and the gate on PATH, so their next push of unquizzed work is still blocked
the natural fix lives in sync, which already runs everywhere and owns the hook lifecycle: remove its own hook when the marker is absent
consciously accepting the stale-hook cost is also a defensible answer, as long as the gap is named
